title: More shoppers know us; fewer pick us once they compare
subtitle: Brand tracker wave 4 (June 2026, n = 2,421). Aided awareness has risen 6 points in a year, mostly from social. But we turn consideration into preference worse than any competitor, and the gap is perceived quality.
summary: Wave 4 of the quarterly brand tracker (n = 2,421) shows aided awareness up to 44%, a 6-point rise over four waves driven mainly by social ads. Only 36% of shoppers who consider us prefer us, the weakest conversion of the four brands tracked. The gap is perceived quality and sustainability, and Competitor C is closing in on our preference share.
key_findings: Aided awareness is 44%, up 3 points since wave 3 (significant) and 6 points since wave 1. 34% of newly aware shoppers first heard of us through social ads.
Only 36% of those who consider us name us as first choice, against 49% for Competitor A and 45% for Competitor C.
We lead competitors on fast, reliable delivery (+9 pts) but trail on quality that lasts (−6), the top driver of preference, and on sustainable materials (−8).
Competitor C's preference share rose from 5.0% to 6.8% over four waves and is now within 0.4 points of ours (7.2%).
